sections.markdown:
## B — Audience, level and prerequisites: general driving: turns, turnabouts, intersections, interchanges, roundabouts and school buses
Audience: every first-time South Carolina Class D applicant; turnabouts and school bus rules matter from the first permit drive and on the skills test.
Why it matters to a first-timer: the left, right, left check and the warning not to trust another driver's turn signal are set out here [A05], along with the road types on which you must stop for a school bus [A09].
Level: a mix of step-by-step procedures (turnabouts) and scenario judgment (who stops for a school bus, when to enter on green).
Prerequisites: the steering and backing skills and the yielding and signal rules from the earlier sections.

corpus_stability.reason: The South Carolina Driver's Manual prints a single edition line (Revised 06/2024) on its front cover; its disclaimer says legislative and SCDMV policy changes may make some content out of date until the agency incorporates them, and a possibly newer unlinked upload exists on the issuer site (freshness debt in the run jams), so the corpus is treated as revised at most about once a year, bound to the registered snapshot.
